subject: chemistry
title: Greenhouse gases and the greenhouse effect
key_idea: Greenhouse gases such as carbon dioxide, methane and water vapour absorb infrared radiation from the Earth's surface and re-emit it in all directions. This warms the Earth and keeps temperatures high enough to support life.

blocks.text: This section covers which gases are greenhouse gases and why they matter.

items.meaning: A gas in the atmosphere that absorbs infrared radiation from the Earth's surface and keeps the Earth warm.
Radiation with a longer wavelength than the radiation that arrives from the Sun.

items: **Water vapour**, **carbon dioxide** and **methane** are greenhouse gases.
They keep the temperature on Earth high enough to support life.
A planet or moon with greenhouse gases in its atmosphere is warmer than one with no atmosphere.
The greenhouse gases are water vapour, carbon dioxide and methane.
They keep Earth warm enough for life.

blocks.text: This section covers the interaction of radiation with the atmosphere, step by step.

items: Short wavelength radiation from the Sun passes through the atmosphere.
The Earth's surface absorbs it and warms up.
The Earth emits longer wavelength radiation, called **infrared radiation**.
Some infrared radiation goes directly into space.
Greenhouse gases **absorb** some of the infrared radiation.
The gas molecules **re-emit** infrared radiation in all directions.
This warms the Earth's surface and the atmosphere.

diagram.alt: Put the steps of the greenhouse effect in order.
diagram.prompt: Put the steps of the greenhouse effect in order.
steps: Short wavelength radiation from the Sun passes through the atmosphere
The Earth's surface absorbs the radiation and warms up
The Earth emits longer wavelength infrared radiation
Greenhouse gases absorb some of the infrared radiation
The gases re-emit infrared radiation in all directions
The Earth's surface and atmosphere become warmer

items: Short wavelength radiation comes in. Longer wavelength infrared radiation goes out from the surface.
Greenhouse gases absorb the infrared radiation and re-emit it, which warms the Earth.

blocks.text: This section covers a common exam link between fuels and the greenhouse effect.

items: Complete combustion of a hydrocarbon fuel makes carbon dioxide and water.
They absorb heat radiated from the Earth and re-radiate it back into the atmosphere.
Burning a hydrocarbon fuel produces carbon dioxide and water vapour.
Both absorb heat radiated from the Earth.

checks.a: Any two from: carbon dioxide, methane, water vapour.

checks.q: Describe what happens to infrared radiation emitted by the Earth's surface.
checks.a: Some goes directly into space. Some is absorbed by greenhouse gases, which re-emit it in all directions and warm the Earth.

checks.q: Explain how methane keeps a moon warmer than a moon with no atmosphere.
checks.a: Short wavelength radiation from the Sun passes through. It is re-emitted from the surface as longer wavelength infrared radiation, which is absorbed by methane in the atmosphere.

exam_phrases: allows short(er) wavelength radiation to pass through (from the sun)
re-emitted from the surface as long(er) wavelength radiation
carbon dioxide / methane which stops radiation escaping
this increases the temperature leading to global warming

mistakes.wrong: Greenhouse gases keep the Earth warm because the ozone layer holds the heat in.
mistakes.right: References to the ozone layer are ignored. Explain with radiation: short wavelength radiation enters, is re-emitted as longer wavelength radiation, and is absorbed by greenhouse gases.

mistakes.wrong: The Sun's radiation is absorbed by methane in the atmosphere.
mistakes.right: The short wavelength radiation passes through. It is absorbed by the Earth and re-emitted as longer wavelength radiation, which is absorbed by the greenhouse gas.
A bare statement earns nothing. If no other mark is given, one mark is allowed for saying methane absorbs longer wavelength (infrared) radiation.

worked_example.question:
Carbon dioxide is a greenhouse gas.

Describe the greenhouse effect in terms of the interaction of short and long wavelength radiation with matter.
answer_points: Short wavelength radiation (ultraviolet) enters the atmosphere.
It is absorbed by materials and re-emitted.
It is re-emitted as longer wavelength radiation (infrared).
The longer wavelength radiation is trapped by a greenhouse gas such as carbon dioxide or methane, which stops radiation escaping.
worked_example.tip: Ultraviolet and infrared are allowed for short and long wavelength radiation. The temperature increases.

exam_phrases: (the gases) absorb heat radiated from earth
re-radiate heat back into the atmosphere

mistakes.wrong: Only carbon dioxide is produced when diesel burns completely.
mistakes.right: Water is also produced. Either carbon dioxide or water earns the first mark, and the formula is allowed.

mistakes.wrong: Carbon dioxide causes the greenhouse effect.
mistakes.right: Add the two linked points: the gases absorb heat radiated from the Earth, then re-radiate heat back into the atmosphere.

worked_example.question:
Diesel oil is a mixture of hydrocarbons that can be obtained from crude oil.

Explain how the greenhouse effect is caused by the gases produced by the complete combustion of diesel oil.
answer_points: The gases absorb heat radiated from the Earth.
They re-radiate heat back into the atmosphere.
worked_example.tip: Traps the heat is allowed. Use the formula of the gas if you prefer.

exam_phrases: energy transferred by radiation from the Sun warms up the Earth's surface
infrared radiation is emitted by the Earth's surface
some infrared radiation goes directly into space
greenhouse gas molecules emit infrared radiation (in all directions)

mistakes.wrong: The ozone layer traps the heat and causes the greenhouse effect.
mistakes.right: References to the ozone layer are not allowed. Describe greenhouse gases absorbing infrared radiation.
The idea of trapping is ignored. Say that greenhouse gases absorb some of the infrared radiation and then emit it in all directions.

worked_example.question:
This question is about the Earth's atmosphere.

Describe and explain what is meant by the greenhouse effect.
answer_points: Energy transferred by radiation from the Sun warms up the Earth's surface.
Infrared radiation is emitted by the Earth's surface, and some goes directly into space.
Greenhouse gases absorb some of the infrared radiation.
Greenhouse gas molecules emit infrared radiation in all directions, warming the Earth's surface and atmosphere.
worked_example.tip: Any three points. Energy is allowed instead of infrared radiation, and a named gas such as carbon dioxide or methane is allowed.
